sections.h2: How does this breathing timer work?
p: Nothing to download and no account to create. The timer runs on this page, on your phone or your computer.
ol: Sit comfortably, with your back straight and your shoulders loose.
Pick a technique, then a length.
Breathe in as the circle grows and breathe out as it shrinks. When it stays still, hold your breath.
p2: The word in the middle tells you what to do, and the number counts down the seconds. You can pause, resume or restart at any time.
Turn on Sound for a very soft note at each change, handy if you like to close your eyes. On most devices, the screen stays on while you breathe.

sections.h2: What is the box breathing technique?
p: Box breathing has four equal sides, like a box. Breathe in for 4 seconds, then hold for 4. Breathe out for 4, then hold again for 4 with your lungs empty.
It is also called square breathing, and it is taught in stress-management courses. Counting four even sides keeps your mind busy, which leaves less room for racing thoughts.
Use it before a meeting, an exam or a difficult call, when you want a clear head.
The timer offers 2, 4 or 5 minutes. It always finishes the cycle you started, so a session can run a few seconds over.
To see when it helps most, read our guide to [box breathing](/en/blog/breathing-exercises-to-calm-down.html).

sections.h2: How does the 4-7-8 breathing technique work?
p: Three steps, always in the same order. Breathe in through your nose for 4 seconds. Hold for 7. Breathe out slowly through your mouth for 8.
Dr. Andrew Weil made this exercise popular. He advises no more than 4 cycles at first, and up to 8 once it feels familiar. Those are the two options in the timer.
Many people use 4-7-8 breathing for sleep, in bed with the lights off. The out-breath lasts twice as long as the in-breath, which makes the whole rhythm very slow.
If holding for 7 seconds feels uncomfortable, stop. Switch to coherent breathing, which has no hold at all.
Coherent breathing is slow and even, with no pause: around 5 to 6 breaths per minute. Some teachers call it resonance breathing. This timer uses 5 seconds in and 5 seconds out.
Breathe through your nose if you can, and let your belly rise and fall. Nothing is forced.

At this pace, your heart speeds up a little as you breathe in and slows down as you breathe out. It is a natural rhythm, and slow breathing makes it more marked. The effect varies from person to person, so go by how you feel.
Choose 3, 5 or 10 minutes. A 5-minute breathing exercise is a good place to start.

sections.h2: Box breathing vs 4-7-8: which one should you choose?
p: They do different jobs. Here is a simple way to decide.
ul: Need focus before something stressful? Try box breathing.
Winding down at night? Try 4-7-8 breathing.
Want a daily habit with no breath holds? Try coherent breathing.
p2: None is better than the others. The right one is the one you find comfortable and come back to.
Our guide to [breathing exercises for meditation](/en/blog/breathing-techniques-meditation.html) goes deeper into each technique.

sections.h2: How long should you practice, and how often?
p: A few minutes is enough. Three minutes every day beats twenty minutes once a month.
ul: Coherent breathing: 5 minutes, up to three times a day.
4-7-8 breathing: 4 cycles, twice a day, for example in the morning and at bedtime.
Box breathing: 2 to 5 minutes, whenever you need it.
p2: Tie it to something you already do: after your coffee, before you open your inbox, when you get into bed.

sections.h2: Is it safe? A few simple precautions
p: These exercises are gentle. Still, listen to your body.
ul: Feeling dizzy, tingly or short of breath? Stop and breathe normally.
Never force a hold. Shorten it, or choose coherent breathing.
Practice sitting or lying down, never while driving or in water.
Pregnant, or living with a heart or lung condition? Check with your doctor first.
p2: This timer is a wellness guide. It does not replace medical advice.

respiration.seances_t: Sessions in the app built around the breath
faq: Are these guided breathing exercises free?
Yes. They are free, with no sign-up and no ads. They run in the browser on your phone or your computer.
Is this the same as the Google breathing exercise?
No, but it works in a similar way. For some searches, Google shows a one-minute breathing exercise in its results. This page adds three techniques, longer sessions and an optional sound.
Should I breathe through my nose or my mouth?
Breathe in through your nose. For box breathing and coherent breathing, breathe out whichever way feels natural. For 4-7-8 breathing, breathe out through your mouth.
Can I do these breathing exercises lying down?
Yes. Sitting keeps you more alert, and lying down is fine at bedtime. Just never practice while driving or in water.
Can I follow the timer with my eyes closed?
Yes. Turn on Sound: a soft note marks each change. It is higher for the in-breath and lower for the out-breath. On iPhone, silent mode mutes the sound, so turn it off first.
Does the breathing timer work offline?
Once the page is open, yes: it no longer needs the internet. To practice anywhere, the MeditaDream app plays offline once your sessions are downloaded.
